pages.x: In 1803 Britain and France went back to war after a single year of peace. The next December Napoleon Bonaparte, the Corsican general who had taken power in France, crowned himself emperor in Notre-Dame, with the pope looking on. Britain paid one alliance of kings after another to fight him.

pages.x: Beethoven had named his new Third Symphony for Bonaparte, the hero of liberty. When he heard that Napoleon had made himself emperor, his pupil remembered, he raged that this was just another tyrant and scratched out the name so hard that he tore a hole in the page. He called it Eroica, the heroic symphony.

In October 1805 Admiral Horatio Nelson attacked the French and Spanish fleets off Cape Trafalgar in Spain, signalling that England expected every man to do his duty. His ships broke through their line and took or wrecked 22 of theirs without losing one. Nelson was shot on his deck and died as the battle was won.

On land, Napoleon tempted the Austrian and Russian emperors into attacking him near Austerlitz in Moravia, then smashed the middle of their line as the sun burned through the morning fog. After this Battle of the Three Emperors, the thousand-year-old Holy Roman Empire was wound up within a year.

Prussia was crushed at Jena in 1806, and in 1807 the tsar made peace with Napoleon on a raft in the middle of the river Niemen at Tilsit. Napoleon made his brothers kings of Holland, Westphalia, Naples and Spain, and tried to starve Britain by closing every port in Europe to its goods.

When Napoleon put his brother Joseph on the throne of Spain in 1808, Madrid rose against the French, and rebels were shot the next day. Francisco Goya painted the firing squad: faceless soldiers, and a man in a white shirt flinging his arms wide. Spain's war of ambushes gave the world a word: guerrilla, little war.

In June 1812 Napoleon led about 600,000 men into Russia. The Russians fell back, burning what they left, and Moscow burned soon after he entered it. No peace was offered, so he turned back as winter came. Starving, frozen and hunted by Cossacks, his army fought its way over the Berezina River in November.

pages.x: Beaten at Leipzig in 1813, Napoleon gave up his throne and was sent to rule the little island of Elba. In 1815 he escaped and marched on Paris, and France rallied to him for a hundred days. On 18 June, near Waterloo in Belgium, the Duke of Wellington's army held out until the Prussians came, and Napoleon's last army broke.

The wars killed millions and ended with Napoleon a prisoner on St Helena, far out in the South Atlantic. But they spread his law code and the idea of the nation across Europe, swept away the Holy Roman Empire and loosened Spain's hold on America, and left Britain the leading power of the century.
